dedupe_keys.name: montreal fire stations earthquake scenario damage assessment for all stations 345 scenarios

description: This case study assessed how every fire station in Montreal would fare in earthquakes, because post-earthquake fires put fire services in high demand just when their buildings may be damaged. Researchers at École de technologie supérieure built a four-part framework: a seismic hazard model using a ground motion prediction equation for Eastern Canada, an inventory that sorts stations into building classes by material and code level, fragility functions for each class, and an impact model that turns damage probabilities into a mean damage state. They ran 345 scenarios varying epicentre and magnitude. For magnitude 6 events, on average 45 percent of stations would suffer at least moderate damage, and the authors derived simple magnitude-damage relationships for planners. The article is free to read and download as open access under CC BY 4.0 in GeoHazards (2025). Coverage is the fire stations of Montreal. Caveats: the station inventory and scenario results are summarised in the article, not published as a separate dataset, and the facts here come from the article abstract. Simulation uses: fire service functionality inputs for post-earthquake fire and emergency response models, and ranking stations for retrofit. Related records: the California fire station retrofit study (case_study-california-fire-station-seismic-retrofit-benefit-cost) takes the next step to benefit-cost analysis.
